title: Matchsticks to Square
statement:
You are given the lengths of `n` matchsticks. Decide whether all of them can be placed together to form a **square**.

Every matchstick must be used **exactly once**. Sticks may not be broken, but they may be joined end to end, so a side of the square can be made of one or several sticks. All four sides must have the same total length.

Print `true` if a square can be formed and `false` otherwise.
inputFormat:
The first line contains the integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers, the matchstick lengths.

examples.explanation: The total is 16, so each side must be 4. Use the sticks {4}, {4}, {2, 2} and {3, 1}.

The total is 16, so each side must be 4. The stick of length 4 can be one side, but each stick of length 3 would need a stick of length 1 to complete its side, and there are none. Joining two 3s gives 6, which is too long.
The total 15 is not divisible by 4, so no square exists.

hints: A square needs a total length divisible by 4, and no stick can be longer than one side. Check these cheap conditions first.
Backtracking: place each stick on one of the four sides, pruning when a side exceeds the target. Trying longer sticks first fails faster.

For a guaranteed bound, use a bitmask over the used sticks. Let dp[mask] be the length of the partly built current side (modulo the side length) after using exactly the sticks in mask, or -1 if mask is unreachable.
